mangalacharan.title: Mangalacharan
mangalacharan.intro: Mangalacharanas are sacred mantras chanted before reading the Gita. It calms our mind and prepares it for knowledge. The word Mangalacharan is derived from the words 'Mangal' (auspicious) and 'Acharan' (behaviour/manner), which symbolizes auspicious beginnings. Since ancient times, this Mangalacharan is recited before reciting Hindu scriptures, so that the recitation is successful and fruitful.
mangalacharan.significanceText:
Mangalacharana is an essential part of Gita recitation. It marks the auspicious beginning of our spiritual journey. Through these mantras we:

• Pray for God's blessings
• Calms and settles our mind
• Pray for wisdom and understanding
• Prepare yourself for the lesson
• Pray for the removal of all obstacles

Ancient sages believed that no scripture reading is complete without Mangalacharana. It ensures sanctity and success of lessons.
mangalacharan.mantraText:
Oh Purnamad: Purnamidang Purnaat Purnamudchyate.
Purnasya Purnamada Purnamevabashisha.

O peace: peace: peace:

Oh Narayanang Namaskritya Narang Chaiva Narottamam.
Debing Saraswating Vyasong Tato Joymudiroyet.

Om Bhadrang Karnevi: Srinuam Deva:
Bhadrang Pashyamakshaviryajatra:
Satiyarangaistushtubamsastanuvhi:
Vyashem devahitang yadayu: ॥

O peace: peace: peace:

section1.title: Purnamad: Mantra
section1.mantra:
Oh Purnamad: Purnamidang Purnaat Purnamudchyate.
Purnasya Purnamada Purnamevabashisha.
section1.meaning:
This mantra speaks of the fullness of God. This means:

'Om' - Symbol of Supreme Being
'Purnmadh' - God is full
'Purnmidang' - This world is also full
'purnat purnamudchyate' - origin of purna from purna
'Purnasya Purnamadaye' - even after taking Purna from Purna
'Purnmebavashishyate' - remains full

Through this mantra we understand that God is full, His creation is also full, and He remains full even after something is taken from Him. It symbolizes God's infinity and omnipresence.

section2.title: Peace Mantra
section2.meaning:
This mantra chants 'Shaanti' three times. The three peaces symbolize the three levels:

• First Shanti – Physical peace (freedom from bodily ailments and sorrows)
• Second Shanti – Peace of mind (Freedom from mental worries)
• Third Peace – Spiritual Peace (Peace of soul and union with God)

By reciting this mantra we pray for peace on all levels.

section3.title: Narayana Namaskar Mantra
section3.mantra:
Oh Narayanang Namaskritya Narang Chaiva Narottamam.
Debing Saraswating Vyasong Tato Joymudiroyet.
section3.meaning:
We salute the three with this mantra:

'Narayanang Namaskritya' - Salutation to Lord Narayana first
'Narang Chaiva Narottamam' - then salutations to Narottama (Shri Krishna).
'Debing Saraswating' - Salutation to Goddess Saraswati (Goddess of Knowledge)
'Vyasong' - Salute to Maharishi Vedavyas (composer of Gita)
'Tato Jayamudiroyet' - Then I started reciting the Gita

Through this mantra we invoke the blessings of all who are required to recite the Gita.

section4.title: Bhadrang Karnevi: Mantra
section4.mantra:
Om Bhadrang Karnevi: Srinuam Deva:
Bhadrang Pashyamakshaviryajatra:
Satiyarangaistushtubamsastanuvhi:
Vyashem devahitang yadayu: ॥
section4.meaning:
This mantra is taken from the Rigveda. This means:

'Bhadrang karnevih srinuyam' - O gods, we hear auspicious words through our ears.
'Bhadrang pashyamakshaviryajatra' - we see auspicious sight with our eyes
'Sthirairangaistustubamsastanuvhi' - we praise you with steady limbs.
'Vyashem devahitang yadayu' - we get long life which is beneficial to the gods

Through this mantra we pray for proper use of our senses and long life and good luck.

mangalacharan.meaningText: Through Mangalacharana we pray to God that our knowledge, intelligence and strength increase and we can walk on the path of truth. These mantras calm our mind, create a spiritual atmosphere and prepare us for reading the Gita. Each mantra has its own significance and together they form a complete prayer that auspiciously initiates our spiritual journey.

mangalacharan.historicalContextText:
The historical context of Mangalacharan is very rich. Mangalacharan is recited before reciting Hindu scriptures since ancient times.

• Vedic Age – Prayers like Mangalacharana were performed even before the recitation of Vedas
• Epic Age – Mangalacharana was recited before reading Ramayana, Mahabharata
• Puranic Age – Mangalacharana was recited even before various Puranic texts
• Modern Age – Mangalacharana is still recited before the reading of Gita, Upanishads and other scriptures.

Maharshi Vedavyas, who composed the Gita, also performed Mangalacharana before his composition. This practice continues today and is an important part of Hinduism.
mangalacharan.spiritualSignificanceText:
The spiritual significance of Mangalacharan is immense. It is not just a ritual, but a deep spiritual practice:

• Connection with God – Through Mangalacharan we establish direct connection with God
• Atmashuddhi – By reciting these mantras our soul is purified
• Mind concentration – our mind is concentrated by reciting Mangalacharana
• Expression of Devotion – Through these mantras we express our devotion to God
• PRAYER OF KNOWLEDGE - By bowing to Goddess Saraswati and Maharishi Vyasa we pray for wisdom
• Auspicious Beginning – Mangalacharana gives an auspicious beginning to our spiritual journey

For all these reasons, Mangalacharana is an essential part of Gita recitation and plays an important role in our spiritual growth.

dhyana.title: meditation
dhyana.introText: Meditation is an important means of spiritual growth. It calms our mind and helps us connect with the soul. The word dhyana comes from the Sanskrit 'dhyai' dhatu, meaning 'to think' or 'to concentrate'. Meditation is deep concentration on the Supreme, through which we can reconcile our soul with the Supreme. Meditation has been used as a major method of spiritual development since ancient times.
dhyana.significanceText:
The importance of meditation is immense. It provides multifaceted benefits in our life:

• Spiritual Development – Through meditation we can reconcile the soul with the Supreme Being
• Peace of Mind – Meditation keeps our mind calm and still
• Physical fitness – Meditation increases our body's immune system
• Mental Health – Meditation helps us reduce stress, anxiety and depression
• Increase concentration – Meditation concentrates our mind and increases efficiency at work
• Confidence – Meditation increases our confidence and helps us face all the challenges of life

Meditation is not only a spiritual practice, but an essential part of our daily life.
dhyana.slokaText:
Dhyanang Paramang Brahmani Satchidanandrupini.
Tasmin dhyatrdhyevain vedo nasti kadachan.

Dhyanang Monsi Sanstapya Paramatmani Chetsa.
Sarvabhuteshu Chaitanya Samang Pasyati Yogi.

Dhyanyogen Monsi Pashanti te Yuganuyugong.
Tasmin dhyatrdhyevain vedo nasti kadachan.
dhyana.slokaMeaningText:
These verses describe the deeper meaning of meditation:

• First verse - Nature of meditation: Meditation is concentration on the Supreme Brahman, who is Satchidanandrupi (the form of Truth, Mind and Joy). When we focus on the Supreme in meditation, there is no distinction between dhyata (the one who meditates) and dheya (the one who is meditated upon).

• Second verse - Results of meditation: When we fix our mind on the Supreme, we see the same consciousness in all living beings. The Yogi sees the same Supreme Being in all beings.

• Third sloka - Vision through meditation: Through meditation we see the Supreme Being in our mind for ages. In meditation there is no distinction between the mind and the mind, we become one with the Supreme.

These verses convey the deep philosophical significance of meditation.
dhyana.meaningText: Meditation is concentration on the Supreme Being. When we sit in meditation, our mind calms down and we feel oneness with God. Through meditation we can reconcile our soul with the divine. It is not only a spiritual practice but it is an essential part of our daily life which improves us physically, mentally and spiritually.
benefits: Mind calms and settles – Through meditation our mind calms down and we find solutions to all problems in life
Slows down thinking – Meditation slows down our thinking and focuses our mind

Physical Fitness – Meditation boosts our body's immune system and improves our physical health
Increases concentration – Meditation concentrates our mind and increases efficiency at work
dhyana.typesText:
There are different types of meditation, each with its own characteristics and benefits:

• Saguna Dhyana – In this meditation we meditate on specific forms or attributes of God. For example - Krishna meditation, Rama meditation etc.

• Nirguna Dhyana - In this meditation we meditate only on the Supreme Being, without any specific form of God. This is a higher level of meditation.

• Breathing Meditation – In this meditation we focus on our breath. It is a simple and effective method of meditation.

• Mantra Meditation – In this meditation we chant a mantra and concentrate on that mantra.

• Chakra Meditation – In this meditation we focus on the different chakras in our body.

Each type of meditation has its own importance and we can follow any method according to our needs.
steps: Choose a quiet and secluded place - Sit in a quiet, clean and secluded place where you can meditate undisturbed.
Sit properly – Sit in Padmasana, Sukhasana or any comfortable asana, keeping your spine straight
Close your eyes - Close your eyes and take deep breaths and calm yourself down
Focus the mind on the breath - Focus your mind on the breath and feel the movement of the breath
When the mind wanders, return to the breath - If your mind wanders, patiently focus on the breath again

dhyana.tipsText:
Some important tips for meditation:

• Time Selection – It is best to meditate in the morning or evening, when the environment is calm
• Location Selection – Select a quiet and secluded location where you can meditate undisturbed
• Regularity – Regular practice is essential to reap the benefits of meditation
• Patience – Mastering meditation takes time, so practice patiently
• Start slowly - Start with 5-10 minutes in the beginning and gradually increase the time
• Comfortable Seat – Choose a comfortable seat so you can sit for long periods of time
• Mind wandering - If your mind wanders, consider it normal and patiently refocus

Following these tips will help you master meditation.
dhyana.historicalContextText:
The historical context of meditation is very rich. Meditation has been used as a major method of spiritual development since ancient times:

• Vedic Age – Meditation is mentioned in the Vedas and was considered a major method of spiritual development
• Upanishad Age – Meditation is described in detail in the Upanishads and was considered a major method of attaining salvation.
• Gita Yuga – Dhyana Yoga is described in detail in the Gita and was considered a major method of spiritual development.
• Buddhist Age – Meditation is an essential part of Buddhism and was considered a major method of attaining nirvana
• Modern Age – Meditation is still used today as a major method of spiritual development and scientific studies have proven its benefits

Meditation is not only an ancient practice, but it is still relevant today and brings positive changes in our lives.
dhyana.spiritualSignificanceText:
The spiritual significance of meditation is immense. It is not just a mental exercise, but a deep spiritual process:

• Reconciliation with the Supreme Soul – Through meditation we can reconcile our soul with the Supreme Soul
• Atmajnana – Through meditation we come to know the true nature of our soul
• Mokshalava – Through meditation we can be liberated from the cycle of birth and death and attain Mokshalava.
• Vision of God – Through meditation we can gain vision of God
• Self-Purification – Through meditation our soul is purified and we get rid of sins
• Enlightenment – Through meditation we can gain deep knowledge and understand the true meaning of life

For all these reasons, meditation is an essential means of spiritual growth and an important part of our lives.

gitaMahatmya.title: Gita-Mahatmya
gitaMahatmya.intro: Gita is the essence of all Vedas. It shows the solution to all the problems of life and the path to spiritual progress. Gita-Mahatmya is a description of the greatness and importance of Gita. It tells us about the infinite power and spiritual value of Gita. Ancient scriptures say that by reading, listening and thinking about the Gita, we can get rid of sin, gain merit and salvation.
gitaMahatmya.significanceText:
Gita-Mahatmya is a detailed description of the glories of Gita. This tells us:

• What benefits can we get from reading Gita?
• What changes come in our lives by listening to Gita
• How our spiritual growth takes place through Gita meditation
• How we can get rid of sin and merit by reading Gita
• How the path to salvation is paved by reading the Gita

Gita-Mahatmya informs us about the infinite power of Gita and motivates us to read Gita.
gitaMahatmya.mahatmyaText:
Srikrishnaarjunasambada in Gitasupanisatsu Brahmavidyayang Yogashastra.
Name of Arjunvishadyoga Prothomohadhyaya:

Gitashastramidang Punyang Yah Pathettang Narottam.
Gnanabairagyasiddharthang Bhakting Kurban Govinde.

Gitaya: Shravanenaiva Samranenaiva or Narah.
Muchyate sarvapapevyo Vishnulokong sa gachti ॥
gitaMahatmya.mahatmyaMeaningText:
The glories of Gita are described in these verses:

• First verse - Introduction to Gita: This is the essence of the Upanishads, Brahmavidya and Yoga Shastra, where the dialogue between Krishna and Arjuna takes place.

• Second sloka - Result of reading the Gita: One who reads this holy Gita Shastra and devotes himself to Lord Govinda for knowledge, Vairagya and Siddhi, becomes Narottam (the best man).

• Third verse - Results of hearing and remembering the Gita: One who only hears or remembers the Gita, is freed from all sins and moves to Vishnu.

These verses reveal the infinite power and importance of Gita.

Enhancement of Knowledge and Intelligence – Reading the Gita enhances our knowledge and intelligence and helps us understand the true meaning of life
Mind calms and settles - By reciting Gita our mind calms and we find solutions to all problems of life
Spiritual growth takes place - Reading the Gita guides us to spiritual growth and we come closer to God
Solution to all the problems of life - Gita gives us the solution to all the problems of life and helps us to follow the right path
The Path to Salvation is Smooth - By reciting the Gita the path to salvation is smooth and we can be freed from the cycle of birth and death.
Removes fear and anxiety - Reading the Gita removes our fear and anxiety and increases our confidence
Shows the Right Path of Karma - The Gita teaches us Niskam Karma and shows the right path of Karma
gitaMahatmya.readingBenefitsText:
Special Benefits of Gita Reading:

• Daily Recitation – Recitation of Gita daily calms our mind and we find solutions to all problems in life
• Listening - Listening to the Gita concentrates our mind and we can take the teachings of the Gita to heart.
• Contemplation – Contemplating the Gita sharpens our intellect and we understand the deeper meaning of life
• Remembrance – Remembrance of Gita keeps the teachings of Gita alive in our mind and we can take right decisions in all situations of life

In all these ways Gita brings positive changes in our lives.
gitaMahatmya.historicalContextText:
The historical context of Gita-Mahatma is very rich. Since ancient times the glories of Gita have been described in various scriptures:

• Narration in Puranas – The glories of Gita are described in detail in various Puranas
• References in the Mahabharata – The origin of the Gita and its importance are described in the Mahabharata
• Support in the Upanishads - Upanishads support the teachings of the Gita
• Modern Age – Even today millions of people are getting spiritual progress through reading Gita

The Gita-Mahatmya tells us that the Gita is not just a scripture, but a complete philosophy of life that is relevant to all ages.
gitaMahatmya.spiritualSignificanceText:
The spiritual significance of Gita-Mahatma is immense. This tells us:

• Infinite Power of Gita - By reading, listening and meditating on Gita we can get rid of sin, gain merit and salvation.
• Elevation of soul – Reading Gita improves our soul and we come closer to the Supreme Soul
• Meaning of Life – Gita helps us understand the true meaning of life and teaches us to follow the right path
• Philosophy of Karma – The Gita teaches us Niskam Karma and shows the right path of Karma
• The Path of Bhakti – The Gita teaches us Bhakti Yoga and shows the path of attaining God through Bhakti
• The Path of Knowledge – The Gita teaches us about Jnanyoga and shows the path to salvation through knowledge

For all these reasons, Gita-Mahatmya informs us about the infinite power of Gita and motivates us to read Gita.

gitaSummary.title: Summary of the Gita
gitaSummary.intro: Gita is a holy book divided into 18 chapters. Each chapter contains deep teachings about different aspects of life. Here is a brief description of the main content of each chapter. The Srimad Bhagavad Gita is a part of the Mahabharata, in which Lord Krishna answers life's deepest questions to Arjuna. It is not just a scripture, but a complete philosophy of life that guides us to spiritual progress through action, meditation, knowledge and devotion.
gitaSummary.significanceText:
Srimad Bhagavad Gita is one of the most important scriptures of Hinduism. It provides solutions to all problems of life:

• Karma Yoga – Spiritual advancement through selfless action
• Jnanyoga - salvation through knowledge
• Bhaktiyoga - Attainment of God through devotion
• Dhyanayoga – self-restraint through meditation

The Gita teaches us what our duty is in every situation of life and how we should walk the right path. It is not only for spiritual development but also guides us in all aspects of daily life.
gitaSummary.structureText:
The Gita is divided into 18 chapters, each dealing with a particular topic:

• First 6 Chapters - Karma Yoga and Importance of Karma
• Next 6 Chapters - Bhakti Yoga and Nature of God
• Last 6 Chapters - Path to Enlightenment and Salvation

In total 700 verses Gita answers all the questions of our life. Each chapter contains deep philosophical thoughts that help us understand the meaning of life.
gitaSummary.importanceText:
The importance of reading the Gita is immense. This is our:

• Helps to understand the true meaning of life
• Teaches proper balance between actions and results
• Speaks of the immortality of the soul and the omnipresence of God
• Teaches observance of religion in all circumstances
• Shows the way to salvation
• Helps keep the mind calm and steady

Daily reading of Gita calms our mind, sharpens our intellect and we find solutions to all problems of life.

In this mantra the word 'Hare' is an invocation to the power of God, 'Krishna' is the giver of supreme bliss and 'Rama' is supreme bliss. Through this mantra we invoke the grace of Lord Krishna by chanting his name.
niyom: Take a bath every morning and wear clean clothes and chant the mantra
Before chanting the mantra, sit in front of a picture or idol of Lord Krishna
Use garlands while chanting mantras (108 chants)
Do not think about anything else while chanting the mantra, just concentrate on the mantra
You can chant the mantra out loud or in your mind while chanting
Maintain devotion and reverence while chanting the mantra
Do not eat meat, fish, egg, onion, garlic while chanting the mantra
Do not smoke and drink alcohol while chanting the mantra
Maintain cleanliness while chanting mantras
Chant the mantra regularly at the same time every day
podhoti: In the morning take a clean bath and take asana

Close your eyes and take deep breaths and calm yourself down
Start chanting the 'Hare Krishna' mantra with the garland in hand
Touch one mala bead with each chant
Chant the mantra 108 times (a garland).
Contemplate the form of Lord Krishna while chanting the mantra
After chanting the mantra meditate for a while
Pray to Lord Krishna after chanting the mantra

Happiness and peace come in life

verseOfTheDay.title: Today's verse
verseOfTheDay.subtitle: An inspirational verse every day
verseOfTheDay.introText: Today's Shloka is a special feature of Gita which brings you a new and inspirational verse every day. A different verse is selected each day, which helps you learn about the deeper teachings of the Gita. These verses will guide you in various situations of life and help in spiritual growth.
verseOfTheDay.significanceText:
The importance of today's verse is immense. This is our:

• Keeps connected with Gita daily - By reading a new verse every day we stay connected with Gita regularly
• Guides Life – Each verse guides us in different situations of life
• Leads to spiritual growth - By regularly reciting shlokas we gain spiritual growth
• Keeps Mind Calm - Reciting one verse daily keeps our mind calm and still
• Increases knowledge – Each verse gives us new knowledge
• Motivates – Each verse gives inspiration in our life and helps us to move on the right path

For all these reasons, today's verse is an important part of our daily life.
verseOfTheDay.benefitsText:

• Connection with Geeta – By reciting shlokas daily we are constantly connected with Geeta
• Increase in knowledge – Each verse gives us new knowledge and sharpens our intellect
• Keeping the mind calm - Reciting shloka daily keeps our mind calm and still
• Spiritual Upliftment – By regularly reciting shlokas we get spiritual upliftment
• Life Guidance – Each verse guides us through different situations in life
• Inspiration – Each verse gives inspiration in our life and helps us to move on the right path

Practice reading today's verse regularly to get all these benefits.
verseOfTheDay.inspirationMessage: Motivate yourself by reading a verse of Gita every day. Each verse will help you understand the deeper meaning of life and guide you to spiritual growth.

allEkadashi.title: All Ekadashi
allEkadashi.intro: Ekadashi is a holy day in the Hindu calendar that falls twice every month - on Krishna Paksha and Shukla Paksha. A total of 24 Ekadashis are celebrated in a year. Each Ekadashi has its own importance and significance. Lord Vishnu is worshiped and fast observed on this day.
allEkadashi.significanceText:
Ekadashi is a very important day in Hinduism. On this day:

• Lord Vishnu is specially worshipped
• Spiritual purification is achieved by fasting
• Get rid of sin
• Spiritual growth takes place
• The mind remains calm and steady
• Improves health

Each Ekadashi has its own name and significance and each has different results.

instructions: Have a light meal in the evening before Ekadashi (Dashmi).
On Ekadashi morning take bath and wear clean clothes
Worship Lord Vishnu and chant the mantra
Observe a complete fast (some people take fruit or milk)
Avoid lying, anger, greed etc
Spend time in meditation and prayer
Read the Gita or chant the Lord's name
On the next day of Ekadashi (Dwadashi) in the morning perform puja and donate to Brahmins
Then take sattvic food
Observe Ekadashi regularly for spiritual upliftment
